facts.claim: Bali charges each foreign tourist a levy of IDR 150,000, paid once while travelling in Bali, before leaving Indonesia.

sources.title: Love Bali (Bali Provincial Government): Tourist levy

articles/where-to-stay-in-bali.html: Every foreign visitor owes Bali's tourist levy of IDR 150,000, once a trip
IDR 150,000 a person, once a trip
paid once while you are in Bali, before you leave Indonesia

facts.claim: The levy is paid cashless via the Love Bali website or app (encouraged before departure), at payment counters at Bali's airport and port, or via registered endpoints (hotels, travel agents, attractions); accepted: Visa, Mastercard, American Express, JCB, bank transfer, virtual account, UnionPay, QRIS; the voucher is emailed with a QR code.

sources.title: Love Bali: About us and regulations

articles/where-to-stay-in-bali.html: Pay it on the official Love Bali website or in the Love Bali app
Payment is cashless, by Visa, Mastercard, American Express or JCB card, bank transfer, virtual account, UnionPay or QRIS
the voucher arrives by email with a QR code

facts.claim: Exempt from the levy: diplomatic and official visa holders, transport crew, KITAS/KITAP holders, family-unification, student and golden visa holders (and other visas on application); cruise passengers pay.

articles/where-to-stay-in-bali.html: Cruise passengers pay too

facts.claim: The levy is governed by Bali Provincial Regulation 6 of 2023 as amended by Regulation 2 of 2025, and Governor Regulation 25 of 2025.
